title: Redis → ElastiCache: DUMP/RESTORE Migration
description: Migrate Redis data from K8s StatefulSet to Amazon ElastiCache using DUMP/RESTORE with minimal downtime.

steps.action: Create ElastiCache Redis cluster (Valkey 8.x or Redis 7.x) in same VPC, cluster mode disabled (or enabled if source uses clustering), encrypted at rest (KMS) and in-transit (TLS)
steps.verify: Cluster status = Available; primary endpoint resolves

steps.action: Export Redis keys from source: redis-cli --rdb /tmp/dump.rdb (or BGSAVE + copy RDB file from K8s pod)
steps.verify: RDB file size matches expected; redis-check-rdb /tmp/dump.rdb passes

steps.action: Upload RDB file to S3: aws s3 cp /tmp/dump.rdb s3://<migration-bucket>/redis/dump.rdb
steps.verify: aws s3 ls s3://<migration-bucket>/redis/ shows file with correct size

steps.action: Restore into ElastiCache using AWS Backup or redis-cli RESTORE (for cluster use redis-cluster-migrate tool or RIOT)
steps.verify: redis-cli -h <elasticache-endpoint> DBSIZE returns same key count as source

steps.action: Update application connection strings to point to ElastiCache endpoint, redeploy pods with new env vars
steps.verify: Application logs show successful cache hits from ElastiCache; latency p99 < 2ms
steps.rollback: Revert env vars to K8s Redis endpoint
